transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello. My wife and my son really pushed me to come in because they say I've been acting all over the place at work and at home. It's like I can't control what I'm doing anymore or keep my behavior appropriate to what's actually going on around me.
Do you ever have thoughts or beliefs that you know are not true, but they feel very real to you, such as thinking people are plotting against you or that you have special powers?

No, I don't have any thoughts like people plotting against me or having special powers. For me, it's more that my thoughts get completely jumbled up and I lose control over how I'm acting or what my body is doing.
Can you describe a specific situation where you felt like your thoughts were jumbled and you lost control over your actions, and how did that affect your daily life or interactions with others?

At work, I tried explaining a schedule issue but got completely sidetracked talking about barcodes turning into patterns, all while pacing in tight circles and flapping my hands. This chaotic behavior got me written up at my job, and now my wife and son can't even trust me to handle basic things at home like paying the bills.
Have you experienced any significant mood swings, such as periods of extreme euphoria or irritability, alongside these episodes of disorganized thinking and behavior?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of extreme highs, euphoria, or severe mood swings. My struggles are really just about the confusion, my thoughts getting all jumbled up, and those odd physical behaviors I can't seem to control.
Can you tell me if you've ever heard voices or seen things that aren't there when no one else is around, which might be different from the jumbled thoughts and loss of control you've described?
No, I definitely haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't there. My struggles are really just about my thoughts getting completely jumbled up and losing control over my physical actions.
Can you describe if these episodes of jumbled thoughts and loss of control over your actions are persistent, or if they come and go, and how long you've been experiencing them?

I started feeling myself gradually coming apart about a year ago when a new inventory system rolled out at work. However, these specific, severe episodes of jumbled thoughts and out-of-control behaviors have been persistent and clearly off the rails for the last six months.
Have you noticed any decrease in your motivation or interest in activities you used to enjoy, alongside these episodes of disorganized thinking and behavior?

No, I haven't really noticed a loss of motivation or interest in the things I do. My main struggles are still just my thoughts getting completely jumbled up and losing control over my physical actions.
Can you tell me more about what happens before these episodes of jumbled thoughts and loss of control, and if there are any specific triggers or events that seem to set them off?

They usually flare up when I'm under a lot of stress at work, especially when I'm trying to explain that complicated new scheduling system or why a shift got messed up. Then, if someone confronts me or tells me to stop pacing, it just makes my physical behaviors worse and I'll start freezing or repeating their words under my breath. It's like my brain gets completely overloaded trying to explain things and I just lose control.

When you're under stress and your thoughts become jumbled, do you feel like you're trying to make sense of things or respond to the situation, or is it more that you're completely disconnected from what's happening around you and just reacting physically?

In my head, those jumbled thoughts actually feel like they connect and make perfect sense at the time, even if others can't follow what I'm saying. Physically, though, I feel completely disconnected from my own body, like I've lost control over the pacing, freezing, or repeating words and can't stop how I'm acting in front of people.
Can you clarify if, during these episodes, you're aware that your thoughts are jumbled and your behavior is inappropriate, or if it's only afterwards that you realize what happened?

During those moments, it's a strange mix of awareness because in my head, everything actually feels perfectly connected and makes complete sense while I'm speaking, even though I notice my mouth won't get back to the point and people are staring. For the physical behaviors, I actually catch myself pacing or freezing right in the moment, feeling completely trapped and out of control while it is happening rather than finding out about it later.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling 'trapped' during these episodes, and do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body while they're happening?

I don't really feel like I'm observing myself from the outside or anything like that. It's more that I just feel a complete loss of control over my physical actions and my speech when these episodes happen, and I can't seem to stop them. That's the only way I feel "trapped"—just being unable to make my body do what I want in the moment.

Can you describe if you've ever had a period where your thoughts were clear and organized, and you were in control of your actions, but then suddenly shifted into one of these episodes of jumbled thoughts and loss of control?

The overall change wasn't a sudden overnight shift, but rather a gradual unraveling over the past year since the new store system was introduced, getting much worse over the last six months. However, on a day-to-day basis during a normal conversation, I do experience sudden, uncontrollable shifts where my thoughts instantly derail into odd patterns like barcodes and I completely lose track of what I was saying.

Can you tell me if, during these episodes of jumbled thoughts and loss of control, you've ever had any fleeting moments where you doubted your own identity, felt like you were someone else, or experienced any other kind of break from reality?

No, I've never doubted who I am or felt like I was someone else. My main struggle is really just getting very jumbled up and losing control of my thoughts and physical actions, exactly as I've described.

Can you clarify if, during these episodes of jumbled thoughts and loss of control, you've ever experienced any brief moments of clarity where you realized your thoughts or behaviors were irrational or not based in reality, even if only for a split second?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't really thought about it that way. When it's happening, everything I'm thinking feels like it makes sense to me at the time, so it's more that I'm just struggling to stay in control of my body and my speech.
Can you think of any times when, after one of these episodes passed, you looked back and realized that your thoughts or behaviors during that time didn't make sense or weren't based in reality?

Yes, looking back later, especially when my wife or coworkers point it out, I do realize how bizarre and completely disconnected from reality I was acting. In the moment, the barcode patterns and my need to pace feel entirely real and uncontrollable, but afterward, I feel deeply embarrassed by how nonsensical and out of control it all actually was.

Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'bizarre and completely disconnected from reality' when you look back on these episodes, and how that realization affects your understanding of what happened during those times?

Actually, I'm not sure I would use the words "disconnected from reality" myself, because when it's happening, those thoughts and actions feel very real and connected to me. It's more that I now recognize I simply wasn't in control of my body or my speech in those moments.

Can you describe if there are any moments, either during or after these episodes, where you question whether your perceptions or interpretations of events are accurate, or if you ever wonder if there's another way to understand what's happening that doesn't involve feeling so out of control?

I have a hard time questioning my perceptions or looking for other explanations because, when it's happening, everything feels completely real and connects perfectly in my head. I am just too overwhelmed by the sudden loss of control over my body and speech to stop and think about it any other way.

Can you think of any instance where you had a clear understanding that your jumbled thoughts or out-of-control behaviors were not based in reality, even if it was just a fleeting moment of insight during or right after one of these episodes?

It's really hard to tell, and I don't think I have that kind of clear insight during those moments. In the middle of it, everything either feels like it makes perfect sense in my head, or I am just completely overwhelmed by losing control of my body.

Can you think of any situation where you realized, either during or immediately after one of these episodes, that your thoughts or behaviors were not grounded in reality, and if so, how did that realization impact your understanding of what was happening?

I don't really have those moments of realization because everything feels like it makes perfect sense to me at the time. I'm just not sure how to answer that, since I don't see it as not being grounded in reality while it's actually happening.
Can you think of any times when you've had thoughts that you knew were unrealistic or not based on real events, but you couldn't stop thinking about them, and how did that affect your behavior?

Yes, I sometimes get completely fixated on thoughts like barcodes on products turning into complex patterns. When I get overwhelmed by these thoughts, my speech gets completely derailed and disorganized, making it hard for others to follow. At the same time, it triggers those physical behaviors like pacing in tight circles, flapping my hands, or freezing up because I just can't stop them.

Can you think of any instance where, after one of these episodes passed, you looked back and realized that not only were your behaviors out of control, but the thoughts driving them were also fundamentally unrealistic or not based in reality?

Looking back, especially when my family points it out, I can see that thoughts like the barcodes turning into patterns were completely unrealistic and bizarre. In the moment, it felt entirely logical and connected in my head, but I now realize how disconnected from reality those moments actually look. It is hard to admit, but those ideas really weren't based in reality.

Can you describe how you feel about the fact that your thoughts and behaviors during these episodes are later recognized by you as unrealistic, and does this realization influence how you try to cope with or manage these episodes in any way?

It's honestly really hard for me to make sense of it all, even when I look back on those episodes. Because they feel so real in the moment, I don't really know how to cope with or manage them yet. That's why I'm here, because I just don't know what to do when it happens.

Can you tell me if there are any specific moments or reflections where you've realized that your jumbled thoughts or behaviors were not only out of control but also not based in reality, and if so, how has that affected your understanding of yourself and these episodes?

During those moments, like when I see barcodes turning into patterns or find myself pacing, it all feels completely real and connected in my head. The realization that I'm out of control usually only hits me when I see other people's confused or concerned reactions, or when I'm repeating words and unable to stop. This makes me feel deeply unsettled and disconnected, as I can't seem to bridge the gap between what makes sense to me and how chaotic it looks to everyone else.

Can you describe how you differentiate between what feels real to you during these episodes and what others tell you is unrealistic or not based in reality, and how do you reconcile these two perspectives?

During those episodes, things like the barcodes forming patterns feel completely logical and connect perfectly in my head at the time. I only realize others see it as unrealistic or strange because of how they stare at me or ask me to stop pacing. I really struggle to reconcile these two perspectives because, in those moments, I feel like I have absolutely no control over my own mind or body.

Can you think of any situation where you had a moment of clarity, realizing that your thoughts or behaviors during one of these episodes were not based in reality, and if so, how did that moment of clarity come to you?

I don't really have those sudden moments of clarity where I realize on my own that my thoughts aren't based in reality, because at the time, everything feels completely connected and real to me. I usually only realize something is wrong because of how my wife or coworkers react to me, or because they have to point it out. Otherwise, in my head, it all makes perfect sense while it's happening.
Can you describe any instance where you felt like your jumbled thoughts or behaviors were not only out of control but also not based in reality, and how did you come to that realization?

This happens quite often, especially when I try to explain simple work tasks and get completely derailed by thinking the barcodes are turning into patterns, all while pacing in circles, flapping my hands, or freezing. I only realized these episodes weren't normal because my coworkers would stare at me like I was speaking total nonsense, and my wife and son eventually had to step in to point out how odd and out-of-control I was acting.

Can you think of any instance where you had a moment, either during or after one of these episodes, where you questioned whether your perceptions or thoughts were truly reflective of reality, even if it was just for a brief moment?

I'm not really sure, to be honest, and I haven't really questioned my thoughts in that way. When it's happening, everything makes complete sense to me in my head, even if it looks completely strange and confusing to everyone else.

Can you think of any times when you were able to recognize, even if briefly, that your thoughts or behaviors during these episodes were not based in reality, and if so, how did you come to that realization?

I don't really have those moments of clarity where I realize what's happening isn't real. At the time, everything makes perfect sense to me or just feels completely out of my control. It's usually only because of my wife, son, or coworkers' reactions that I realize something was off.

Can you think of any instance where you were able to step back and recognize that your jumbled thoughts or out-of-control behaviors were not only chaotic but also not grounded in the real world, even if it was just for a brief moment?

I don't really have those moments of stepping back. When these things happen, it either feels completely connected and real in my head at the time, or I just feel entirely out of control of my body without being able to analyze it.

Can you think of any situation where you realized, either during or immediately after one of these episodes, that your thoughts or behaviors were not only out of control but also not based in reality, and if so, how did that realization impact your understanding of what was happening?

I'm not really sure, as I haven't had a clear moment of realizing my thoughts weren't based in reality. While it's happening, everything makes complete sense to me. I only realize something is wrong because of how out of control I feel physically and because of the worried reactions of my family and coworkers.
